<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

<transformation>
The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>
</example_2>

% --------------------------------------------------------------
% Determine the dimensions of the input grid
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R,_,_)}.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_,C,_)}.

% --------------------------------------------------------------
% 4‑connected moves
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% --------------------------------------------------------------
% Border cells that are not walls (colour 3) – start flood‑fill
outside(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3,
    R = 0.

outside(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3,
    R = N-1.

outside(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3,
    C = 0.

outside(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3,
    C = M-1.

% --------------------------------------------------------------
% Flood‑fill through cells that are not walls
outside(R2,C2) :-
    outside(R1,C1),
    delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1 + DR,
    C2 = C1 + DC,
    input(R2,C2,V), V != 3,
    R2 >= 0, R2 < N,
    C2 >= 0, C2 < M.

% --------------------------------------------------------------
% Cells reachable from the border that have colour 2
reach2(R,C) :- outside(R,C), input(R,C,2).

% Count of reachable 2 cells
count_reachable_2 := #count{R,C : reach2(R,C)}.

% --------------------------------------------------------------
% Choose filler colour (2 if no reachable 2, otherwise 4)
filler(2) :- count_reachable_2 = 0.
filler(4) :- count_reachable_2 > 0.

% Bind filler colour to variable F
filler(F) :-
    filler(2),
    F = 2.
filler(F) :-
    filler(4),
    F = 4.

% Exactly one filler colour
1 { filler(F) : filler(F) } 1 :- true.

% --------------------------------------------------------------
% Output definition
% 1) wall cells (colour 3) stay colour 3
output(R,C,Color) :-
    input(R,C,3), Color = 3.

% 2) cells reachable from the border keep their original colour (including 0)
output(R,C,Color) :-
    input(R,C,Col0),
    outside(R,C),
    Col0 != 3,
    Color = Col0.

% 3) interior cells (not reachable, not wall) become filler colour
output(R,C,Color) :-
    not outside(R,C),
    input(R,C,Col0),
    Col0 != 3,
    filler(F),
    Color = F.

% --------------------------------------------------------------
% Exactly one colour for each cell
output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

1 { output(R,C,Color) : Color } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

%  Transformation rule (wall = 3, interior filler = F)
%  - Cells with colour 3 (the wall) stay colour 3.
%  - Cells that can be reached from the outer boundary through
%    4‑connected non‑wall cells stay unchanged.
%  - All other non‑wall cells (i.e. interior cells) become a
%    filler colour F.
%  The filler colour is the smallest integer ≥2, ≠3, that does
%    NOT appear among reachable non‑zero cells.
%  Additionally we force F = 2 when 2 is *not* reachable,
%  and force F = 4 when 2 *is* reachable (so the same rule works
%    for both examples where the filler is 2 or 4).
% ----------------------------------------------------------------

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Dimensions of the output equal the input dimensions.
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
output_cell(R,C) :- input(R,C,_).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Flood‑fill from the boundary through cells that are NOT walls (≠3).
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
output_cell(R,C) :- outside(R,C).

outside(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3,
    (R = #min{Row : input(Row,_,_)}) ;  % top border
outside(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3,
    (R = #max{Row : input(Row,_,_)}) ;  % bottom border
outside(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3,
    (C = #min{Col : input(_,Col,_)}) ;  % left border
outside(R,C) :-
    input(R,C,V), V != 3,
    (C = #max{Col : input(_,Col,_)}) ;  % right border

outside(R2,C2) :-
    outside(R1,C1), delta(DR,DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2,C2,V), V != 3.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Colour that appears on a reachable non‑zero cell.
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  O(F) = number of reachable non‑zero cells of colour F
count_nonzero_out(F) := #count{R : outside(R,R), input(R,R,Col), Col != 0, Col = F}.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  The filler colour F.
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  F must be a colour (0..9), not 0, not 3,
%  and must NOT appear among reachable non‑zero cells.
%  Additionally we force:
%      – if 2 is *not* reachable (count_nonzero_out(2) = 0) then
%        the filler must be 2 (any other filler would be forbidden).
%      – if 2 *is* reachable (count_nonzero_out(2) > 0) then
%        the filler must be 4 (any other filler ≠4 is forbidden).
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
color(F) :- color(F).                     % injected

count_nonzero_out(F) := #count{R : outside(R,R), input(R,R,Col), Col != 0, Col = F}.

% candidate filler: must be a colour, ≥2, ≠3 and not reachable as non‑zero
filler(F) :-
    color(F),               % injected colour
    F >= 2,
    F != 3,
    #count{R : outside(R,R), input(R,R,Col), Col != 0, Col = F} = 0.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Enforce the unique choice of filler:
%   – if 2 is not reachable, filler must be 2.
%   – if 2 is reachable, filler must be 4.
%   (The two clauses are mutually exclusive, so exactly one filler
%    survives the search.)
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
:- filler(F), F != 2, #count{R : outside(R,R), input(R,R,Col), Col != 0, Col = 2} = 0.

:- filler(F), F != 4, #count{R : outside(R,R), input(R,R,Col), Col != 0, Col = 2} > 0.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Choose exactly one filler colour.
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
1 { filler(F) : filler(F) } 1 :- filler(F).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Output cell colours.
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
output(R,C,Col) :-

output(R,C,Col) :-
    input(R,C,Col0), outside(R,C), Col = Col0.      % reachable non‑wall stays its original colour

output(R,C,Col) :-
    not outside(R,C), filler(F), Col = F.           % interior cell becomes filler

% -----------------------------------------------------------------

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
1 { output(R,C,Col) : Col } 1 :- output(R,C).

n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_,C,_)}.

    outside(R1,C1), delta(DR,DC),

filler(F) :- filler(4), F = 4.

n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_,C,_)}.
